title: Throughput-Latency Interaction Matrix for Heterogeneous Request Mix
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Construct a high-resolution interaction matrix that maps throughput (tokens/sec) to tail latency (p95/p99) across realistic heterogeneous request mixes to identify batching and queueing interference regimes and actionable mitigation knobs.
background: Continuous batching and internal queueing introduce non-linear interactions under mixed tenant workloads. Recent customer reports and internal dashboards show occasional p95 regressions coincident with high bursty traffic from small, latency-sensitive sessions. We need reproducible experiments that combine multi-class arrival profiles, KV cache locality variance, and model-sequence-length heterogeneity to surface stable decision boundaries for autoscaler and router policies.
objective: Produce a reproducible test suite and a parameterized matrix visualization that answers: 1) At what aggregate tokens/sec and queue depth do p95 and p99 jump for a given mix? 2) How do batching size distributions and KV hit ratios change the tipping points? 3) Which runtime knobs (aggressive dequeue rate, max-batch cap, adaptive time-slicing) delay the tipping points with acceptable cost tradeoffs?
success_criteria: Deliver a reproducible harness that can sweep throughput, mix ratio (latency-sensitive vs throughput-oriented), and KV hit rates
Publish an interaction matrix visualization with annotated tipping points and 95% CI for p95/p99 across cells
Recommend 2 actionable runtime policy changes with quantified token-cost impact and latency benefit
Add automated regression detectors that trigger when p95 degrades by >15% at a fixed tokens/sec compared to baseline
Document test artifacts and include GitHub CI jobs to run a reduced sweep nightly
approach: Define canonical tenant classes: small-LLM chat (short seq, latency-sensitive), long-gen (long seq, throughput-oriented), embedding-batch (high tokens/sec but tolerant latency)
Implement arrival generator that can emit Poisson, bursty (Weibull), and scheduled spikes with per-tenant class weights
Instrument runtime to export live batch_size distribution, queue_depth histogram, KV cache hit/miss ratio, tokens/sec, p95/p99, and per-request trace ids
Run factorial sweeps: throughput (10%,25%,50%,75%,100% of capacity), mix ratio (0/25/50/75/100%), KV hit (20/50/80%), model sequence length distributions
Create visualization pipeline that computes per-cell median and 95th percentile bands and automatically flags cells where p95 increases superlinearly with throughput
Iterate on runtime knobs (max_batch_size, dequeue_timeout, per-tenant priority boost) and re-run targeted sweeps to measure benefits and cost delta
test_matrix: Throughput sweep: [100 tps, 300 tps, 600 tps, 1200 tps] normalized to baseline GPU capacity
Arrival patterns: [steady Poisson, diurnal + microbursts, synchronized bursts]
metrics_to_capture: cost per 1M tokens estimate for each knob configuration
detection_rules: Regression alert when p95 at fixed throughput increases >15% relative to baseline cell
Anomaly if batch_size median drops >30% while queue_depth increases >20% (indicates throttling interference)
SES (statistical equivalence) test between baseline and candidate runs with alpha=0.01 for p95
Automatic triage link created with latest visual matrix when a nightly job flags a regression
progress_updates: 2025-02-12: Initial specification drafted and reviewed with runtime team. Agreed canonical tenant classes and metrics list.
2025-02-18: Arrival generator prototype committed. Basic Poisson and burst modes implemented. PR opened: #182
2025-02-21: Instrumentation hooks added to serving runtime. Exporters for batch_size and queue_depth landed in runtime-telemetry PR #290
2025-02-25: Completed first small-scale sweep against 1-GPU dev harness. Observed early tipping point at ~420 tps for mix 50/50 with KV hit 20%
2025-03-01: Visualization prototype completed and posted to dashboard. Identified promising knob: per-tenant priority boost delays tipping by ~18% with +6% token cost
blockers: Need extended GPU lab time to run full factorial sweep at cluster scale; quota request in progress
Telemetry ingestion pipeline lacks per-trace sampling consistent across runs; working with observability to add deterministic sampling flag
risks: Nightly full-sweep runs are costly and could impact other lab usage — may need billing approval
Behavior observed in dev harness may not fully match multi-GPU production due to inter-GPU scheduling differences
Detection thresholds tuned on synthetic mixes might produce false positives for some customers with atypical traffic patterns
